request.question: What are the three levers to recover C1?

answer:
**C1 cash cost rose from USD 20.16/t in Q4 FY2026 to USD 21.33/t last quarter (Q1 FY2027), and the three biggest levers to recover it are Maintenance (+0.67 USD/t), Volume (+0.27 USD/t), and Diesel Efficiency (+0.24 USD/t).**

## Cost bridge Q4 FY2026 → Q1 FY2027

| Lever | Impact (USD/t) | Description | Source |
|-------|----------------|-------------|--------|
| **Maintenance** | **+0.67** | Fleet maintenance & maintenance-order cost per tonne rose beyond the volume effect | Stand-in cost postings |
| **Volume** | **+0.27** | Fixed costs spread over fewer tonnes (4.74 Mt → 4.58 Mt) | FMS, historian |
| **Diesel Efficiency** | **+0.24** | Diesel litres per tonne increased (queue time, haul distance) | FMS haul cycles |
| Tyre Wear | +0.12 | Tyre cost per tonne rose | Stand-in cost postings |
| Price | −0.04 | Unit prices (diesel, explosives, power, rail, port) fell slightly | Stand-in cost postings |
| Other | −0.09 | Other inputs and fixed cost changes | Stand-in cost postings |
| **Total change** | **+1.18** | Q4: 20.16 → Q1: 21.33 USD/t | MIXED |

The Maintenance spike (fleet maintenance rose from 2.07→2.10 USD/t and maintenance orders from 0.27→0.94 USD/t) is the clear outlier.

**Recommended action:** Investigate the maintenance-order surge in Q1 FY2027—review work orders, unplanned breakdowns, and fleet availability to understand the 3.5× jump in that cost element.
